_README: Licence registry for licence_provenance.py. Seeded 2026-08-09.
RULE: an entry appears here ONLY when its licence was read at the primary
source (the LICENSE file or the vendor's legal page), and 'source' records
where. A weight that is absent from this file classifies as UNKNOWN, which is
NOT a pass. That is deliberate and is the whole design: guessing 'probably
fine' into this file converts an unread licence into a green gate, which is
the exact failure mode the gate exists to prevent.
'commercial': true = licence permits commercial use.
'commercial': false = it does not.
'commercial' absent = not established -> UNKNOWN.
'territory_excluded': territories where the licence forbids use OF THE OUTPUTS.
'families' keys are the model_family values the LoRA trainer writes into
training_status_<family>.json. A character LoRA is charged with its BASE
model's licence, because a LoRA is a derivative work of the model it was
fine-tuned from.

2026-10-05: every path in a 'source' or 'note' field is written against a NAMED
ROOT from zyg_workflows.paths — 'ZYG_MODELS_ROOT/gnm/LICENSE' and never one
machine's home directory — so this file reads the same on every box.
licence_provenance.resolve_root_path() expands the roots; a field that
still carries an absolute path keeps working and is returned unchanged.

klein.note: FLUX.2 [klein] 4B. ONLY the 4B is Apache-2.0 — verified via the HF model_info cardData on both black-forest-labs/FLUX.2-klein-base-4B and .../FLUX.2-klein-4B. _lora_lineage_README: Maps a LoRA NAME or staged sub-folder to the base family it was fine-tuned
from, for LoRAs whose lineage cannot be read off the filesystem.
This exists because char_id is NOT a lineage key. One character has several
LoRAs trained on DIFFERENT bases for different stages: an image LoRA on
wan_char_<id> by char id finds the FLUX leg and charges a licence that weight
never touched - a false FAIL on every VACE graph in the repo.
Checked AFTER exact path evidence (lora-weights-<family>/ or a status file
pointing at this exact file) and BEFORE the ambiguous char-id fallback.

lora_lineage.note: Wan video LoRAs. lora_attest._SEED_GLOBS pins the same two folders as the identity-deciding weights.
SDXL identity LoRAs. Listed before the flux rule so the family suffix wins over the broad flux glob.

FLUX image LoRAs. Deliberately does NOT match the BARE zygchar_<id>.safetensors: arcane_restyle.py:112 stages the SDXL LoRA under that exact name while comfy_generation_service.py:1385 stages family-suffixed ones, so the bare name is a two-writer collision with no family in it. Bare names fall through to the char-id scan and are charged the worst of the character's legs - honest ambiguity beats a coin-flip in either direction.

Character LoRAs trained on the undistilled FLUX.2 klein-4B base. The first version of this rule matched zygchar_klein_* — a name nothing ever writes; the stager emits zygchar_<cid>_<family>, so a staged klein LoRA fell through to the char-id scan and was charged the worst of the character's OTHER legs (FLUX). Fixed before any klein LoRA existed.

DELIBERATELY UNRESOLVED - 'commercial' is absent so this classifies UNKNOWN, not cleared. The model card says 'free to use for personal and creative work under CreativeML Open RAIL-M' and separately that it 'may not be deployed behind paid API services' without licensing, directing commercial enquiries to juggernaut@rundiffusion.com. It does not state whether commercially PUBLISHING OUTPUTS (a monetised video channel) counts as the commercial use requiring that licence - we deploy nothing behind an API. That is the exact question to put to RunDiffusion; do not resolve it by guessing here.

ICT FaceKit — ICT Face Model LIGHT: 26,719-vertex topology, 100 identity PCA modes, 53 ARKit-named expression morph targets. Code and shape data are the SAME grant here because the morph targets are repo content, not a separately-licensed weight drop. Scope is deliberately the light model only. The FULL ICT model is not in this clone; README:188 states it 'will be released under a different USC specific license', so it is UNKNOWN and must be registered separately if it is ever fetched. data/assets/ict_facekit/PROVENANCE.json carries the full licence text and the file hashes.

NOTICE lists exactly four third-party components: dinov2 (Apache-2.0) and TRELLIS.2 / Direct3D-S2 / MoGe (MIT), and states Pixal3D imposes no restriction beyond the originals. File-level grep over *.py/*.txt/*.md for EUROPEAN UNION|Territory|non-commercial|Hunyuan returns NOTHING. The HF repo is NOT gated. OPEN QUESTION, unresolved: the model card metadata carries extra_gated_eu_disallowed: true, which is inert while gating is off but is a statement of intent by the publisher; re-read the card before ANY re-download or update, because flipping gating on would make this an EU-territory exclusion. sha256 pins below are HuggingFace's published LFS digests for the files actually fetched (the MV geometry + texture set only; the four single-view checkpoints were not downloaded).

The image conditioner Pixal3D actually loads. Read at file level: section 1(a) grants a worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, reproduce, distribute, copy, create derivative works of and modify the materials. The string 'commercial' appears NOWHERE in the licence, so there is no non-commercial clause; the only mention of the European Union is inside the definition of Sanctions, which is a trade-controls clause, not a territory exclusion. No restriction on outputs. Redistribution must carry the agreement, which does not bind us: the operator never distributes tools. OPEN QUESTION, unresolved: the canonical repo facebook/dinov3-vitl16-pretrain-lvd1689m is gated:manual and our token is refused (HTTP 401), so the weights actually on disk came from camenduru/..., a third-party mirror whose own card metadata still carries Meta's gating form. The licence text is the same; the ACCEPTANCE is not. Before production use the operator should request access on the facebook/ repo and re-fetch from it. sha256 of the fetched weight file, HuggingFace's published LFS digest: dcb2e45127cccbf1601e5f42fef165eea275c8e5213197e8dcf3f48822718179 (model.safetensors, 1212559808 bytes), repo commit 3c276edd87d6f6e569ff0c4400e086807d0f3881.

_rejected_README: Components EVALUATED and REJECTED on licence grounds, with the sentence that
disqualified each one. Recorded so a rejection is not re-litigated in six
months by someone who only remembers that 'we looked at SVC once'.
This section is documentation: attest_licences() does not read it.

rejected.name: Applio / RVC
rejected.evaluated_for: singing-voice conversion — make one of the 294 bank voices sing
rejected.reason: The MIT repo ships ZERO weights. It FETCHES checkpoints at runtime that are sha256-identical to a project whose own licence reads 'research use only' and which explicitly binds anyone who disseminates exported voices. An MIT wrapper around non-commercial weights is non-commercial.

rejected.name: DiffSinger / DDSP-SVC / so-vits-svc
rejected.reason: All three default to the openvpi NSF-HiFiGAN vocoder, whose checkpoints are CC BY-NC-SA. The vocoder is literally what emits the published samples, so the NC term attaches to the output, not to a build-time tool.

rejected.name: YingMusic-SVC
rejected.reason: MIT code over cc-by-nc-4.0 weights. Same shape as Applio.

rejected.name: Open singing corpora (Opencpop, M4Singer, GTSinger, OpenSinger, Kiritan)
rejected.evaluated_for: training a clean SVC model from scratch
rejected.reason: EVERY open singing corpus is non-commercial. This is not a shopping problem and will not be solved by looking harder. Building a corpus from IndexTTS-2 output is also closed: its licence section 3.4(c) bars using outputs to improve a commercial AI model.

rejected.name: ACE-Step 1.5 ReferenceTimbreAudio
rejected.evaluated_for: using a bank voice as the singer via the reference input
rejected.reason: Verified by executing the real code: supplying a reference sets is_covers=True, drops the audio codes and makes the reference the SOURCE LATENT. It is a cover path. A 10 s donor on a 60 s song is silence-padded bit-exactly for 83% of the track, and in a live A/B a 98 Hz male donor produced the HIGHEST output pitch of any condition (309 Hz). Not a licence rejection — a capability one.

rejected.name: DWPose (the ComfyUI Wan-Animate tutorial's own preprocessor)
rejected.evaluated_for: per-frame 2D skeleton for the Wan2.2-Animate pose_video input
rejected.reason: Already on this house's banned list and the ban holds on inspection: DWPose distills from a COCO-WholeBody-trained teacher and its released weights inherit the dataset's non-commercial terms. The official ComfyUI tutorial wires it by default, which is exactly why S06 draws the skeleton with MediaPipe through geom/keypoints.detect instead — same OpenPose colour and bone convention as geom/char_vace, no DWPose node anywhere in _comfy_workflows/wan22_animate.json.

rejected.name: FLUX.1-Kontext-dev (the Wan-Animate --use_flux retarget)
rejected.evaluated_for: retargeting the driver's proportions onto the reference character
rejected.reason: Non-commercial FLUX.1 [dev] licence family, and the whole FLUX.1-dev family was deleted from this box in the 2026-08-25 disk audit. Not wired. When proportions need retargeting the reference is to be rendered from the character's own registered body (S05 geom/body_plates.py) instead.

rejected.name: Wan2_2-Animate-14B_fp8_e4m3fn_scaled_KJ.safetensors (the INITIAL upload)
rejected.evaluated_for: the weights S06's brief names by exact filename
rejected.reason: Licence is identical (same repo, Apache-2.0); the objection is technical and comes from the vendor. Kijai's own Wan22Animate/README.md says the initial uploads keep the face-encoder layers in bf16, and that in NATIVE ComfyUI those layers 'get downscaled to normal fp8, which seems to introduce pretty bad noise in a grid pattern', which the _v2 files fix. S06's graph is the native one, so the initial file is the wrong file for it. The v2 of the SAME precision (e4m3fn) was taken instead; the one-precision-only rule is kept.

rejected.note: Registered as an explicit DENY before anything can download them. FLAME 2020, MICA, EMOCA, SMIRK and the Basel Face Model are the obvious reference heads for a landmark fitter and every one of them is research/non-commercial. rejected.name: pymomentum (PyPI)
rejected.evaluated_for: decoding MHR parameters back to a posed mesh, so a pose track can re-synthesise every frame under one locked identity
rejected.reason: Meta's pymomentum (facebookresearch/momentum, the solver mhr.mhr.MHR imports) is distributed through conda/pixi and has no PyPI release under that name. The PyPI project literally named `pymomentum` is pyMomentum 0.1.4 by Momentum Teknoloji AS — an SMS-gateway client library (MIT, modules pyMomentum.sms.providers.mutlucell / sanalsantral), unrelated in every way. Downloaded the sdist and read PKG-INFO before installing anything: `pip install pymomentum` in the body venv would have silently added a third-party SMS package to the environment that decodes human body geometry. Not installed. `pymomentum-gpu`, which the plan named, does not exist on PyPI at all (pip index: 'No matching distribution found').
rejected.consequence: geom.pose_track cannot re-pose the rig, so its shape lock is RECORDED and measured, never applied — track.json carries shape_lock_applied=false and the reason. Downstream geometry (geom.track_plates) rasterises the estimator's own per-frame pred_vertices instead, which needs no decoder.
rejected.reopen_if: Meta publishes pymomentum to PyPI under a name whose LICENSE and repository can be read at file level, or the box grows a conda/pixi environment that can host it beside torch 2.13 cu126.

rejected.note: This is the rembg_model named in Pixal3D's shipped pipeline.json / pipeline_mv.json, and pixal3d/pipelines/pixal3d_image_to_3d.py:123 instantiates it UNCONDITIONALLY at from_pretrained time — so running Pixal3D as shipped downloads and loads a non-commercial matting model even when every input already carries alpha. S10 therefore runs with a local pipeline_mv_norembg.json that drops the rembg_model key, and patched that line to tolerate its absence.
